questions.q: In 'The Wild Boar and the Fox', why did the Boar sharpen his tusks when there was no danger?
choices: When danger comes there will be no time to get ready
He was bored and had nothing better to do that day
He wanted to scare the Fox away from his tree
His tusks were broken from fighting another boar
questions.evidence: when danger does come there will not be time for such work as this

questions.q: In 'The Ass, the Fox, and the Lion', what did the Fox secretly promise the Lion?
choices: To lead the Ass into a pit
To bring him a fat chicken
To leave the forest for good
To help him fight the Ass
questions.evidence: I will lead that foolish creature yonder into a pit

questions.q: What is the lesson of 'The Ass, the Fox, and the Lion'?
choices: Traitors may expect treachery
Lions always keep their promises
Always hide in a pit from danger
Foxes make the best of friends

questions.q: In 'The Birds, the Beasts, and the Bat', what did the Bats do during the war?
choices: Joined whichever side was winning
Fought bravely for the Birds
Fought bravely for the Beasts
Tried to make peace between them
questions.evidence: when they saw the Birds getting the better of it, they were Birds

questions.q: In 'The Birds, the Beasts, and the Bat', why do Bats fly out only at night?
choices: Birds and Beasts drove them out for being deceitful
Their eyes are too weak to see in bright daylight
They love to fly by the light of the moon and stars
They hunt for Mice that only come out at night
questions.evidence: Birds and Beasts made common cause to drive out the Bats

questions.q: In 'The Lion, the Bear, and the Fox', what happened after the Lion and Bear were too hurt to fight?
choices: A Fox ran off with the kid
They shared the kid fairly
The kid got up and ran home
A hunter caught both of them

questions.q: In 'The Wolf and the Lamb', why couldn't the Lamb have muddied the Wolf's water?
choices: The Lamb was downstream and the Wolf was upstream
The Lamb had not been drinking from the stream at all
The water in the stream was much too deep to muddy
The Lamb was standing on a dry rock far from the water
questions.evidence: you are upstream and I am downstream

questions.q: What is a lesson of 'The Wolf and the Lamb'?
choices: A tyrant can always find an excuse
Always drink upstream from a wolf
Wolves are fair and careful judges
Never tell lies about others
questions.evidence: The tyrant can always find an excuse for his tyranny.
